text:
Ah, the primary material of a candle. It is, of course, wax. But let us not be so pedestrian as to simply call it "wax." In the grand theater of adulthood, wax is merely the solidified form of our unfulfilled potential, slowly melting away under the warm, flickering glow of our own mediocrity.

Just as a candle burns down to nothing, so too does our enthusiasm for "spontaneity" evaporate the moment we realize that choosing between chicken and beef instant noodles is the most daring decision we will make all week. We stand before the pantry, a beacon of adult agency, only to be paralyzed by the sheer magnitude of flavor profiles available in a cardboard box. This is not indecision; this is the pinnacle of executive leadership.

And what of the long-term planning? Oh, the sheer audacity of it! We map out our futures with the precision of a military strategist, only to conclude that our five-year plan involves watching the same three seasons of a show we’ve already seen, while simultaneously complaining about the structural integrity of our lumbar region. The candle burns, the noodles boil, and the back pain sets in. It is, truly, a magical journey.
